Instead, we should only increase orders at the most downstream node (node0) to meet demand, while keeping upstream nodes at their HAPPO orders to avoid over-ordering. Node0 has a large backlog (66) and its pipeline is 76, which is relatively high, so increasing its order may not help immediately. However, node0's backlog is the largest contributor to cost. We propose a small increase at node0 only when its backlog is high and its pipeline is not too high, to avoid excessive pipeline. For node1 and node2, we keep orders unchanged to prevent upstream backlog. This rule is conservative and aims to reduce downstream backlog without increasing total cost.
